payload.headline: Apple edges up 0.43% to 355.58, still above every value estimate

summary.thesis: Apple is a strong, cash-rich business, but at 355.58 the price assumes faster growth than Apple is showing, while forecasts keep slipping.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for a lower price. Swing: wait for a breakout or a pullback that holds.
summary.act_at: Long-term buy at 300.56, add at 273.18; swing only above 361.9 or on a hold of 347.89–351.46

payload.happening: Apple closed at 355.58, up 0.43%. It sits in a price zone of 354.04–356.18, just under resistance at 359.76–361.9. There has been no news since the last note, and the next earnings report is on 2027-01-28.
payload.business: The business itself is in good shape. Sales over the last twelve months were 478.8B, up from 416.2B. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) rose to 136.1B from 98.8B. The operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) improved to 33.01% from 31.97%. Two things need watching. First, growth is slowing: quarterly sales growth was 11.72%, down from 16.6% two quarters ago. Second, the filings show inventory up 154% while quarterly sales rose 12%. Unsold product can force price cuts, which would hit margins. That is a real business risk, and the 2027-01-28 report will be the first test of it. The new risk on an investigation in the annual report is a governance and sentiment issue for now. It does not change demand or cash today. Analysts have trimmed their forecasts: next-quarter EPS fell to 2.15 from 2.24, a 3.8% cut. Debt of 80.1B is larger than cash of 36.3B, leaving net debt of 23.4B. That is small next to 136.1B of yearly free cash flow, so the balance sheet is not at risk.

worth.text: Every method puts fair value below today's price. A discounted cash flow model (today's value of future cash) gives 145.37 in the bear case, 202.38 in the base case and 265.87 in the bull case. Apple's own price-to-sales history gives 222.1 to 300.56. To justify 355.58, free cash flow would need to start growing at about 26.9% a year. Last year's sales grew 15%, and sales grew 8% a year over three years. At 20% starting growth the value is 273.18. It only reaches 399.83 at 30%. The stock trades at 39.6 times trailing earnings and 33.5 times next year's expected earnings. Its price-to-sales ratio is 10.8, against a peer median of 5.2, and sits at the 98th percentile of its own five-year range. If the operating margin fell to 24%, value would drop to 204.49. The gap between the methods comes down to one thing: how fast cash flow grows in the early years.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow has to start growing at about 26.9% a year to support the price, far above the 15% sales growth of last year.

bull: Free cash flow jumped to 136.1B from 98.8B a year earlier, so the business is throwing off more cash.
Operating margin rose to 33.01% from 31.97%, and the share count fell 1.56% in a year, which lifts each share's slice of profit.
The trend is up: the price is above the rising 50-day average of 342.84, with higher highs and higher lows.
bear: The price needs about 26.9% starting cash-flow growth, but sales grew 15% last year and 8% a year over three years.
Price-to-sales of 10.8 is about twice the peer median of 5.2 and at the 98th percentile of Apple's own five-year history.
Inventory is up 154% against 12% sales growth, and next-quarter EPS forecasts were cut 3.8% in 30 days.

levels.what: Today's close. It is above the whole value range of 145.37–300.56, so it is too high to buy.
The top of the fair-value range and of Apple's own price-to-sales history, near the 200-day average of 303.96. Buying starts here.
The value if free cash flow starts growing at 20%, which is still faster than last year's 15% sales growth. Adding makes sense here.

longterm.why: The business is high quality, but the price assumes growth Apple is not showing, and forecasts are falling. The rule verdict is 'Too expensive' and the committee call is Hold.

swing.why: Resistance at 359.76–361.9 is closer than one typical daily move (ATR, average true range) of 8.56, and the macro read is negative. Enter only on a close above 361.9, or on a pullback that holds support at 347.89–351.46.

decision.timing: Options price a 4.9% move by 2026-12-18 and a 10.5% move by 2027-02-19, a window that includes the 2027-01-28 report. There is no long-term buy above 300.56 before that report shows whether the inventory build hurt margins.

change_mind: A close above 361.9 would clear resistance and turn the swing call to enter, with support at 347.89–351.46 as the stop zone.
A pullback to 300.56 would turn the long-term call to buy, and a drop to 273.18 would turn it to add.

If the 2027-01-28 report shows the operating margin holding near 33.01% and the next-quarter EPS forecast rising back above 2.24, the slowdown worry eases. If the margin heads toward 24%, value falls to 204.49 and the range stays well below the price.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait on both horizons, because the close of 355.58 remains above the top of the value range at 300.56 and below resistance at 359.76.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
